guards.note: Three independent defects, any one fatal. (1) spawn(npx.cmd, {shell:false}) is rejected by Node >= 18.20.2 (CVE-2024-27980) — and it threw at the VITE spawn, at module scope OUTSIDE the try, so nothing cleaned up. (2) waitForPort probed 127.0.0.1 while vite binds ::1: after fixing (1) it still timed out at 30s while vite was serving. (3) kill() spawned taskkill asynchronously and every caller follows it with process.exit(), so the wrapper died first and left an orphan on [::1]:3499 that broke the NEXT run through --strictPort. Class note: never falsely green, just loudly and permanently red — which is why it survived. ADR-0073 and measure-pt-compile.mts had both written it down as a platform fact.

summary.headline: The two items the brief flagged as highest-risk were both worse than suspected, and in the opposite direction to the rest of the sweep. smoke:all was PERMANENTLY RED — four members pointed at vite's stock port 5173 while this repo pins 3400, so it died at member 28 and FOURTEEN of its 42 never ran, among them smoke:interact, which CLAUDE.md lists as an automated check. Behind that port sat two members that had rotted undisturbed: one reading an absolute path into the dev/ tree deleted 2026-06-17, one asserting UI copy that exists nowhere in the repo. None of those four had an npm script of its own. And smoke:with-server could not execute a single line of its job on this platform — spawn EINVAL at module scope — a breakage so old that ADR-0073 and a harness comment had both written it down as a platform fact. Neither ever went falsely green; both were loudly, permanently red, which is exactly why they survived.
summary.chainingVerdict: HEALTHY, falsified in all four positions. FIRST: 1s, exit 1, only member 1's output — it short-circuits. MISSING member: 1s, exit 1, ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — not skipped. MID (28 of 42): exit 1 through 27 successful predecessors. LAST (42 of 42): exit 1 after 581s and 782 lines, through all 41. Nothing is swallowed. The last was only testable AFTER the port repair — before it, the exit contract of this script's entire tail was unreachable.

sweepComplete.gateVersusTool: This is the number that says how much the repo actually guards, and it is high. Of the 75, essentially all are genuine gates that can move an exit status. The exceptions, each identified as such by the batch that swept it, are FIVE: test:frag:scan ('a report, not a guard'), test:dither ('a metrics lab, not a test' — since repaired INTO a gate), test:compat:write (a snapshot writer), smoke:screenshot (a visual capture) and smoke:with-server (a process wrapper). smoke:tsaa is a sixth borderline case — batch 8 found it to be a boot canary plus a screenshot capture rather than the TSAA guard its name implies, and repaired the canary half. So roughly 93% of the sweep's surface is gate rather than tool, and the failure mode the sweep kept finding was never 'this is not really a test' — it was a real gate with an assertion a vanished, blank, zeroed or default subject satisfied.
sweepComplete.defectRate: 44 of 75, a shade under 60%. Batch 9b's three are the last of them, and they broke the pattern: all three were red-and-ignored rather than green-and-blind.
sweepComplete.notOnTheWORKLIST: Worth knowing, because it bounds the claim. package.json carries 91 guard-shaped scripts today (including the four this batch created). NINE real guards were never on the sweep's worklist and have never been falsified by it: smoke:boot, smoke:undo, smoke:fluid-brush, smoke:fluid-presets, smoke:fluid-toy, smoke:fractal-toy, smoke:migrations, smoke:gx-handles and test:palette. Eight of the nine are members of smoke:all so are at least exercised; smoke:gx-handles is not. So the sweep is complete against its worklist, and the worklist was not the whole of package.json.

lessonsCarriedForward: A GUARD THAT IS LOUDLY RED CAN HIDE LONGER THAN ONE THAT IS FALSELY GREEN.
